The frontend is live and healthy at **https://43110-iv5max7n2co1yuf7e509v.e2b.app/**.

Setup summary:
- Installed frontend (`system/frontend`, npm) and backend (`system/backend`, pip venv) dependencies in parallel — both succeeded.
- Launched the React frontend with `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider npm start` on port 8080, which is confirmed healthy (HTTP 200).

**Limitation:** This app has two independent services — the React UI (port 8080, now running) and a Flask API backend (port 8090, per `system/backend/base.py` and the frontend's `proxy` setting). My tooling manages a single foreground web server per preview, so the backend isn't started. The UI will load, but any action that calls the API (login, loading problems, test cases, chat with LLM agents, etc.) will fail until the backend is also running separately. No API key is required just to start the backend (`openai` is only used when actual LLM calls are made), so you could run it yourself in a second terminal with `cd system/backend && .venv/bin/python base.py` if you want full functionality tested outside this managed preview.

The frontend is live and healthy at **https://43110-iv5max7n2co1yuf7e509v.e2b.app/**.

Setup summary:
- Installed frontend (`system/frontend`, npm) and backend (`system/backend`, pip venv) dependencies in parallel — both succeeded.
- Launched the React frontend with `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider npm start` on port 8080, which is confirmed healthy (HTTP 200).

**Limitation:** This app has two independent services — the React UI (port 8080, now running) and a Flask API backend (port 8090, per `system/backend/base.py` and the frontend's `proxy` setting). My tooling manages a single foreground web server per preview, so the backend isn't started. The UI will load, but any action that calls the API (login, loading problems, test cases, chat with LLM agents, etc.) will fail until the backend is also running separately. No API key is required just to start the backend (`openai` is only used when actual LLM calls are made), so you could run it yourself in a second terminal with `cd system/backend && .venv/bin/python base.py` if you want full functionality tested outside this managed preview.
